title: Finite Kishore conjecture for ratios of Lommel polynomials
statement:
Let $R_{m,\nu}(x)$ denote the Lommel polynomials, and define the coefficient normalization by

$$
\frac{R_{m,\nu+2}(x)}{R_{m+1,\nu+1}(x)}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{N^{(m)}_{n,\nu}}{D^{(m)}_{n,\nu}}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^{2n+1},
$$

where

$$
D^{(m)}_{n,\nu}=\prod_{k=0}^{m}(\nu+k+1)^{f(m,n,k)},
$$

and

$$
f(m,n,k)=\begin{cases}\max\left(\left\lfloor\frac{n+1}{k+1}\right\rfloor,\left\lfloor\frac{n+m-2k+1}{m-k+1}\right\rfloor\right),&k\ne m/2,\\1,&k=m/2.\end{cases}
$$

**Finite Kishore conjecture.** $N^{(m)}_{n,\nu}$ is a polynomial in $\nu$ with nonnegative integer coefficients. This finite version would imply Kishore's theorem, as stated in the paper; the supplied text gives no evidence of a resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08120

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).
source_name: Jang Soo Kim and Dennis Stanton, “Ratios of Hahn–Exton q-Bessel functions and q-Lommel polynomials”, arXiv:2006.08120 (2021).
